ko_meaning_en: A word for counting years

tokens.note: 은 marks the topic; 일 년 sounds like [일련]
열둘 becomes 열두 before a counter

form.q_en: Pick the right number for 'one year'.
form.why: 년 is counted with Sino-Korean numbers: 일 년, 이 년. Native 한/하나 are not used with 년.

ko_meaning: 일 년의 열두 달을 말할 때 쓰는 말
ko_meaning_en: A word used to name the twelve months of a year

form.q_en: How do you say 'June'? (My birthday is in June.)
form.why: June is 유월: 육 drops its ㄱ before 월. October is likewise 시월, not 십월.

ko_meaning: 몇 시인지 시간을 말할 때 쓰는 말
ko_meaning_en: A word used to tell what hour it is

form.q_en: Pick the right number for 'seven o'clock'.
form.why: Hours use native numbers: 일곱 시. Sino-Korean 칠 is used for minutes, as in 칠 분.

ko_meaning: 시간의 작은 단위, 육십 분이 한 시간
ko_meaning_en: A small unit of time; sixty minutes make one hour

tokens.note: 셋 becomes 세 before a counter

form.q_en: Pick the right number for '3:10'.
form.why: Minutes use Sino-Korean numbers: 십 분. Native 열 is for hours, as in 열 시.

ko_meaning_en: Each day; on all days

example.en: My younger sibling drinks milk every day.

form.q_en: Say 'every day' correctly.
form.why: 매일 is an adverb, so it takes no particle: 매일 마셔요, not 매일에.

ko_meaning_en: A place where people live

tokens.note: 에 marks the place where someone is

form.q_en: Pick the particle for 'at home'.
form.why: 있다 'to be (somewhere)' uses 에 for the place. 을/를 mark objects, and 의 means 'of'.

ko_meaning_en: A place where students learn from teachers

form.q_en: The child studies at school. Pick the particle.
form.why: 에서 marks the place where an action (studying) happens. 에 is for where you go or where something is.

ko_meaning_en: A place where people work to earn money

example.en: My older sister goes to the office in the morning.

form.q_en: My older sister works at a company. Pick the particle.
form.why: 에서 marks where an action (working) happens. 에 is for where you go, as in 회사에 가요.

ko_meaning: 아픈 사람을 의사가 고쳐 주는 곳
ko_meaning_en: A place where doctors treat sick people

example.en: Grandpa went to the hospital yesterday.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for 'to the hospital'.
form.why: 가다 uses 에 for the destination; 에서 is for where an action happens. 가/를 only follow a vowel, and 병원 ends in a consonant.

ko_meaning_en: A place that sells things

example.en: I buy bread at the shop.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the particle for 'at the shop'.
form.why: 에서 marks where an action (buying) happens. 을/은 are forms for after a consonant, but 가게 ends in a vowel.

ko_meaning_en: A place where you pay and eat meals

example.en: I eat lunch at a restaurant with a friend.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the particle for 'at a restaurant'.
form.why: Eating is an action, so the place takes 에서. 를 is only used after a vowel, and 식당 ends in a consonant.

ko_meaning_en: A place where you keep or take out money

example.en: There is money in the bank.

tokens.note: 에 marks the place where something is

form.q_en: Ask 'Where is the bank?' Pick the particle.
form.why: 은행 ends in a consonant, so the subject particle is 이 (가 follows a vowel). 을/를 mark objects.

ko_meaning_en: A place where many kinds of goods are bought and sold

example.en: There are a lot of people at the market.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for 'at the market'.
form.why: 에 marks the place where something is: 시장에. 을/를 mark objects, and 가 cannot follow a consonant.

ko_meaning: 사람들이 쉬거나 놀 수 있는 넓은 곳
ko_meaning_en: A large open place where people can rest or play

example.en: The dog plays in the park.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the right form of 놀다 'to play'.
form.why: 놀다 has ㅗ in its stem, so it takes -아요: 놀아요.

ko_meaning: 책을 읽거나 빌릴 수 있는 곳
ko_meaning_en: A place where you can read or borrow books

example.en: The student reads a book at the library.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the particle for 'at the library'.
form.why: Reading happens at the library, so use 에서. 가/를 only follow a vowel, and 도서관 ends in a consonant.

ko_meaning: 지금 있는 곳에서 다른 곳으로 움직이다
ko_meaning_en: To move from where you are to another place

example.en: I'm going to the sea tomorrow.

tokens.note: present tense can describe a plan

form.q_en: I went to the sea yesterday. Pick the past form.
form.why: 어제 needs the past tense. 가 + 았어요 shortens to 갔어요.

ko_meaning_en: To move from another place to here

example.en: My friend comes to my house.

form.q_en: Pick the right present form of 오다.
form.why: 오 + 아요 shortens to 와요.

ko_meaning: 사람이나 물건이 어디에 자리하다, 또는 가지다
ko_meaning_en: For a person or thing to be in a place; or to have something

tokens.note: with 있다, what you have takes 이/가

form.q_en: Pick the particle for 'a dog' in 'Grandma has a dog'.
form.why: With 있다 'to have', the thing you have takes 이/가, not 을/를. 개 ends in a vowel, so 가.

en: to not be there; to not have
ko_meaning_en: To not be there; to not have

form.q_en: Say 'I don't have time today.'
form.why: The opposite of 있다 is its own word, 없다. Korean does not say 안 있어요 for 'don't have'.

ko_meaning_en: To make your home in a place and spend your life there

form.q_en: Pick the particle for 'in Korea'.
form.why: 살다 takes 에 for the place you live (에서 also works). 살다 has no object, and 가/를 only follow a vowel.

ko_meaning: 밤에 눈을 감고 몸과 마음이 쉬다
ko_meaning_en: To close your eyes and let your body and mind rest, usually at night

form.q_en: The baby doesn't sleep at night. Pick the word that makes the verb negative.
form.why: To make a verb negative, put 안 right before it: 안 자요.

ko_meaning_en: To open your eyes and wake up from sleep

example.en: My older brother gets up at six every day.

form.q_en: My brother got up at six today. Pick the past form.
form.why: 일어나 + 았어요 shortens to 일어났어요.

ko_meaning_en: To make your body or things clean with water

example.en: My younger sibling washes their hands.

form.q_en: Politely ask someone: 'Please wash your hands.'
form.why: After a stem ending in a consonant, -(으)세요 becomes -으세요: 씻 + 으세요.

ko_meaning_en: To put clothes on your body

example.en: My older sister wore pants today.

form.q_en: Which thing do you 입다 'wear'?
form.why: 입다 is for clothes worn on the body, like 바지. A hat uses 쓰다 and shoes use 신다.

ko_meaning_en: To rest your bottom on a chair or the floor

form.q_en: Pick the right present form of 앉다.
form.why: 앉 has ㅏ, so it takes -아요: 앉아요. The spelling keeps ㅈ, even though it sounds like [안자요].

ko_meaning_en: To take in people or things with your eyes

example.en: I watch a movie on the weekend.

form.q_en: I watched a movie yesterday. Pick the past form.
form.why: 어제 needs the past tense. 보 + 았어요 shortens to 봤어요.

ko_meaning_en: To take in sounds with your ears

example.en: My younger sibling listens to music.

tokens.note: irregular: ㄷ → ㄹ before a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the right present form of 듣다.
form.why: 듣다 is irregular: ㄷ changes to ㄹ before a vowel, so 듣 + 어요 = 들어요.

ko_meaning_en: To express your thoughts out loud with your mouth

form.q_en: Pick the right present form of 말하다.
form.why: 하다 verbs always become -해요 in the present: 말하다 → 말해요.

ko_meaning_en: To look at writing and understand its meaning

example.en: Grandpa reads the newspaper every day.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for 'the newspaper'.
form.why: 신문 is the object and ends in a consonant, so it takes 을 (를 follows a vowel).

ko_meaning_en: To put letters down with a pencil or pen

form.q_en: Pick the right present form of 쓰다.
form.why: 쓰다 drops ㅡ before -어요: 쓰 + 어요 = 써요.

ko_meaning_en: To learn and practice things you don't know

form.q_en: Say 'I want to study Korean.'
form.why: -고 싶어요 attaches straight to the stem: 공부하 + 고 싶어요.

ko_meaning: 돈을 벌기 위해 어떤 일을 하다
ko_meaning_en: To do a job to earn money

example.en: The doctor works at the hospital.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: The doctor worked at the hospital yesterday. Pick the past form.
form.why: 하다 verbs make the past with 했어요: 일하다 → 일했어요.

ko_meaning: 다른 사람과 같은 곳에서 얼굴을 보다
ko_meaning_en: To see another person face to face in the same place

example.en: I meet a friend on Saturday.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for 'a friend'.
form.why: In Korean, 만나다 takes an object: 친구를 만나요. 친구 ends in a vowel, so 를, not 을.

ko_meaning_en: To give money and get something

example.en: I bought flowers for Mom's birthday.

tokens.note: 의 'of' is often dropped: 엄마 생일 = Mom's birthday

form.q_en: Pick the past form of 사다.
form.why: 사 has ㅏ, so it takes -았어요, and 사 + 았어요 shortens to 샀어요.

ko_meaning: 내 물건을 다른 사람이 가지게 하다
ko_meaning_en: To let another person have something of yours

form.q_en: Pick the right present form of 주다.
form.why: 주 + 어요 shortens to 줘요.

en: to be big; to be tall
ko_meaning_en: To be larger or taller than usual

form.q_en: Pick the right present form of 크다.
form.why: 크다 drops ㅡ before -어요: 크 + 어요 = 커요.

ko_meaning_en: To be smaller or shorter than usual

form.q_en: Pick the right present form of 작다.
form.why: 작 has ㅏ, so it takes -아요: 작아요.

en: to be many; to be a lot
ko_meaning_en: For a number or amount to be more than usual

example.en: I have a lot of homework today.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for 'homework'.
form.why: 많다 describes the subject, so use the subject particle; 숙제 ends in a vowel, so 가.

en: to be few; to be little
ko_meaning_en: For a number or amount to be less than usual

example.en: There are few people in the library.

form.q_en: Pick the right present form of 적다.
form.why: 적 has ㅓ, not ㅏ or ㅗ, so it takes -어요: 적어요.

ko_meaning: 한쪽 끝에서 다른 쪽 끝까지가 멀다
ko_meaning_en: For the distance from one end to the other to be great

form.q_en: Yesterday's class was long. Pick the past form.
form.why: 길다 has ㅣ in its stem, so it takes -었어요: 길었어요. 길어요 is present tense.

ko_meaning_en: To be nice and pleasing

form.q_en: Say 'I like kimchi' with an object (김치를).
form.why: 좋다 cannot take an object (을/를). With 김치를, use 좋아하다: 좋아해요.

ko_meaning_en: To not be good

form.q_en: Pick the right present form of 나쁘다.
form.why: 나쁘다 drops ㅡ. The syllable before it (나) has ㅏ, so it takes -아요: 나빠요.

ko_meaning_en: To look nice; to be lovely to look at

example.en: My older sister's clothes are pretty.

form.q_en: Pick the right present form of 예쁘다.
form.why: 예쁘다 drops ㅡ. The syllable before it (예) has no ㅏ or ㅗ, so it takes -어요: 예뻐요.

ko_meaning_en: To be enjoyable and make you feel good

form.q_en: Pick the particle for 'studying'.
form.why: 재미있다 describes the subject, so 공부 takes the subject particle; it ends in a vowel, so 가.

ko_meaning: 할 일이 많아서 쉴 시간이 없다
ko_meaning_en: To have so much to do that there is no time to rest

form.q_en: Dad was busy yesterday. Pick the past form.
form.why: 바쁘다 drops ㅡ and takes ㅏ (from 바): 바빠요, and in the past 바빴어요.

ko_meaning: 그날의 비, 바람, 해 같은 하늘의 상태
ko_meaning_en: The state of the sky that day, such as rain, wind and sun

form.q_en: Pick the particle for 'the weather'.
form.why: 날씨 ends in a vowel, so the subject particle is 가 (이 follows a consonant). 를/을 mark objects.

ko_meaning_en: For the air to feel hot to your body

form.q_en: Pick the right present form of 덥다.
form.why: 덥다 is irregular: ㅂ becomes 우 before -어요, so it is 더워요.

ko_meaning_en: For the air to feel cold to your body

form.q_en: It was very cold yesterday. Pick the past form.
form.why: 춥다 is ㅂ-irregular: 추워요 in the present, 추웠어요 in the past. 어제 needs the past.

ko_meaning_en: To be slightly warm in a pleasant way

form.q_en: Pick the right present form of 따뜻하다.
form.why: 하다 words become 해요 in the present: 따뜻하다 → 따뜻해요.

en: to be cool; to be refreshing
ko_meaning_en: To be pleasantly cool

form.q_en: Pick the particle for 'the wind'.
form.why: 바람 ends in a consonant, so the subject particle is 이, not 가. 을/를 mark objects.
